questions.question: Choose the correct article: He is ___ honest officer.
questions.explanation: Use 'an' before the vowel sound at the beginning of 'honest'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: We visited ___ Taj Mahal last year.
questions.explanation: Names of unique monuments commonly take the definite article 'the'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: Neither Rani nor her friends ___ present.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb commonly agrees with the nearer subject, 'friends'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: Each of the books ___ a different cover.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes 'has'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: The quality of these mangoes ___ excellent.
questions.explanation: The head noun 'quality' is singular; 'of these mangoes' is a modifying phrase.

questions.question: Choose the correct tense: I ___ my assignment before the teacher arrived.
questions.explanation: The past perfect marks the earlier of two past actions.

questions.question: Choose the correct tense: She usually ___ to school by bus.
questions.explanation: The simple present expresses a regular habit; 'she' takes 'goes'.

questions.question: Choose the correct tense: Look! The dog ___ after the ball.
questions.explanation: The present continuous describes an action happening now.

questions.question: Choose the correct tense: They ___ the museum twice this month.
questions.explanation: The present perfect is suitable for experience within a time period continuing to the present.

questions.question: Choose the correct tense: By the time we reached the station, the train ___.
questions.explanation: The past perfect shows that the train left before we reached the station.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: The children are fond ___ music.
questions.explanation: The expression is 'fond of'.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: He apologized ___ being late.
questions.explanation: The verb 'apologize' is followed by 'for' when giving a reason.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: The meeting begins ___ 10 a.m.
questions.explanation: Use 'at' with a specific clock time.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: My birthday is ___ July.
questions.explanation: Use 'in' with months.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: The picture is hanging ___ the wall.
questions.explanation: Use 'on' for something attached to or displayed on a surface.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: This is the student ___ won the prize.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject relative pronoun referring to a person.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: The artist ___ paintings were displayed is famous.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' expresses possession.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: The person to ___ I spoke was helpful.
questions.explanation: In formal grammar, 'whom' is used as the object of the preposition 'to'.

questions.question: Choose the correct determiner: There isn't ___ milk left.
questions.explanation: 'Milk' is uncountable, so 'much' is appropriate.

questions.question: Choose the correct determiner: Only ___ students answered all the questions correctly.
questions.explanation: 'Students' is countable plural; 'a few' means a small number.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative: This route is ___ than the highway.
questions.explanation: The comparative form of the short adjective 'short' is 'shorter'.

questions.question: Choose the correct superlative: Of the three plans, this is the ___.
questions.explanation: Use 'most practical' as the superlative form.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: The patient feels ___ today.
questions.explanation: 'Well' can function as an adjective meaning in good health.

questions.question: Choose the correct adverb: The athlete ran ___.
questions.explanation: The adverb 'quickly' modifies the verb 'ran'.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: Please speak ___; the baby is asleep.
questions.explanation: The adverb 'quietly' describes how to speak.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: You will succeed ___ you work consistently.
questions.explanation: 'If' introduces the condition for success.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: ___ she was nervous, she delivered the speech well.
questions.explanation: 'Although' introduces a contrast.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: Hurry up, ___ you will miss the bus.
questions.explanation: 'Or' introduces a warning about an alternative consequence.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: He studied hard ___ he could pass the examination.
questions.explanation: 'So that' introduces purpose.

questions.question: Choose the correct modal: You ___ not park here; it is prohibited.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition.

questions.question: Choose the correct modal: ___ I borrow your dictionary for a moment?
questions.explanation: 'May I...?' is a polite way to ask permission.

questions.question: Choose the correct modal: You ___ see a dentist if the pain continues.
questions.explanation: 'Should' expresses advice.

questions.question: Choose the correct modal: When she was five, she ___ already read simple books.
questions.explanation: 'Could' expresses past ability.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive form: The workers clean the classrooms every day.
options: The classrooms are cleaned every day.
The classrooms were cleaning every day.
The workers are cleaned every day.
questions.explanation: The simple present passive is formed with 'am/is/are + past participle'.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive form: The manager will announce the results tomorrow.
options: The results will be announced tomorrow.
The manager will be announced the results.
questions.explanation: The future passive is 'will be + past participle'.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive form: Someone was following us.
questions.explanation: The past continuous passive is 'was/were being + past participle'.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech: Meena said, 'I have finished my work.'
options: Meena said that she had finished her work.
Meena said that I have finished my work.
Meena says she finished her work tomorrow.
Meena said that she has finish her work.
questions.explanation: In reported speech with a past reporting verb, 'have finished' usually backshifts to 'had finished'.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech: He said to me, 'Are you ready?'
options: He asked me was I ready.
He asked me if I was ready.
He told me that are you ready.
He asked that I am ready.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported using 'if' or 'whether' and statement word order.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported command: Mother said to me, 'Do not waste food.'
options: Mother told me do not waste food.
Mother advised me not to waste food.
Mother said me not waste food.
Mother told that I did not waste food.
questions.explanation: A negative command can be reported with 'told/advised + object + not to + verb'.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag: She can swim, ___?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'can' takes the negative tag 'can't she'.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag: They weren't late, ___?
questions.explanation: A negative statement takes a positive tag; the auxiliary is 'were'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He has been working here for 2022.
questions.explanation: Use 'since' with a starting point and a present-perfect form for a continuing situation.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: 'Discuss' takes a direct object and does not normally require 'about'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We entered into the room quietly.
We entered to the room quietly.
We entered in the room quietly.
questions.explanation: 'Enter' is normally transitive and takes a direct object without 'into' in this usage.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: The usual expression for skill is 'good at'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She is married with a doctor.
She is married to a doctor.
She is marry to a doctor.
questions.explanation: The conventional construction is 'married to someone'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have less books than you.
I have fewer books than you.
I have fewest books than you.
I have lesser books than you.
questions.explanation: Use 'fewer' with countable plural nouns such as 'books'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Use 'many' with countable plural nouns.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The scissors is on the table.
The scissors are on the table.
The scissor are on the table.
The scissors has on the table.
questions.explanation: 'Scissors' is normally treated as a plural-only noun and takes 'are'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A pair of shoes are missing.
A pair of shoes is missing.
A pair of shoe are missing.
questions.explanation: The head noun 'pair' is singular, so it takes 'is'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Ten kilometres are a long distance to walk.
Ten kilometres is a long distance to walk.
Ten kilometres have a long distance.
questions.explanation: A measurement considered as one total amount commonly takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The new policy will ___ all employees.
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The medicine had an immediate ___.
questions.explanation: 'Effect' is a noun meaning result.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The teacher gave us a useful ___.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is the noun; 'advise' is the verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: Please ___ me about the schedule change.
questions.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb meaning to inform or recommend.

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'separate'.

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'necessary'.

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'privilege'.

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'environment'.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'diligent'.
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means showing careful and persistent effort.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'tranquil'.
questions.explanation: 'Tranquil' means calm and peaceful.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'commence'.
questions.explanation: 'Commence' means begin.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'obstacle'.
questions.explanation: An 'obstacle' is something that blocks progress.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'optimistic'.
questions.explanation: 'Pessimistic' expresses the opposite outlook to 'optimistic'.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'generous'.
questions.explanation: 'Stingy' means unwilling to give or share.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'transparent'.
questions.explanation: 'Opaque' means not allowing light through; it contrasts with 'transparent'.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'temporary'.
questions.explanation: 'Permanent' means lasting or intended to last indefinitely.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'spill the beans' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means disclose secret information.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'cost an arm and a leg' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means cost a great deal of money.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'get cold feet' mean?
questions.explanation: It means lose confidence or become apprehensive before an action.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'keep an eye on' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means watch something carefully.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of 'metaphor'.
questions.explanation: A metaphor describes one thing as another to suggest a comparison.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of 'simile'.
questions.explanation: A simile makes a comparison using words such as 'like' or 'as'.

questions.question: Which sentence contains personification?
options: The wind whispered through the trees.
questions.explanation: The wind is given the human action 'whispered'.

questions.question: Which sentence contains alliteration?
questions.explanation: The repeated initial /s/ sound creates alliteration.

questions.question: Which sentence is an example of a hyperbole?
options: I have told you a million times.
The book is on the desk.
questions.explanation: Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration for emphasis.

questions.question: Which activity best practises intensive reading?
options: Study a short passage closely for details, vocabulary and structure
Read many texts rapidly for pleasure only
Search a timetable for one time
Listen to a song without focusing on words
questions.explanation: Intensive reading involves close, detailed examination of a text.

questions.question: Which activity best practises extensive reading?
options: Read a longer, accessible story for overall meaning and enjoyment
Analyze every suffix in one sentence
Memorize a list of grammar definitions
questions.explanation: Extensive reading emphasizes reading larger amounts for general understanding and enjoyment.

questions.question: A learner reads a passage to find a person's name. Which reading skill is being used?
questions.explanation: Scanning is used to locate a specific item of information.

questions.question: A learner quickly reads a newspaper article to understand its main point. This is:
questions.explanation: Skimming means reading quickly for the overall idea.

questions.question: Which is the clearest example of making an inference?
options: Conclude that a character is worried from her trembling hands and repeated questions
Copy a date printed in the passage
questions.explanation: An inference combines clues in the text with reasoning to reach a conclusion.

questions.question: Which question checks understanding of an author's purpose?
options: Why did the author write this passage?
How many lines are on the page?
questions.explanation: Author's purpose concerns the reason for creating the text.

questions.question: Which pre-reading strategy activates prior knowledge?
options: Ask learners what they already know about the topic
Require a full written summary before reading
Ask learners to copy the final paragraph
questions.explanation: Activating prior knowledge helps learners connect new information with existing knowledge.

questions.question: Which post-reading activity encourages personal response?
options: Discuss how the text connects with learners' experiences
questions.explanation: Connecting a text with personal experience encourages a response beyond literal recall.

questions.question: Which activity best develops listening for sequence?
options: Arrange picture cards in the order events are heard
Write a synonym for the title
questions.explanation: Ordering events according to what is heard checks comprehension of sequence.

questions.question: Which activity best develops listening discrimination?
options: Identify whether two spoken words begin with the same sound
Summarize a long story from memory
Write an essay on a new topic
questions.explanation: Sound discrimination involves noticing differences or similarities between speech sounds.

questions.question: Which teacher action supports listening comprehension before playing a recording?
options: Introduce the context and set a clear listening purpose
Give the transcript and ask learners not to listen
Ask learners to memorize the recording
Correct spelling before revealing the topic
questions.explanation: Context and a listening purpose help learners focus on relevant information.

questions.question: Which activity primarily develops pronunciation awareness?
options: Listen to and compare minimal pairs such as 'ship' and 'sheep'
Write a summary of a story
questions.explanation: Minimal-pair work draws attention to contrasts between speech sounds.

questions.question: Which is a productive language skill?
questions.explanation: Speaking is productive because learners create spoken language.

questions.question: Which is a receptive language skill?
questions.explanation: Reading is receptive because learners interpret written language.

questions.question: Which task provides a genuine purpose for speaking?
options: Role-play asking for directions to a local place
Repeat a grammar rule without context
questions.explanation: Asking for directions gives learners a practical communicative purpose.

questions.question: Which activity is most suitable for practising polite requests?
options: Role-play borrowing an item using expressions such as 'Could I...?'
questions.explanation: Role-play provides a context for practising request forms and appropriate politeness.

questions.question: Which writing task is an example of functional writing?
options: Write a notice announcing a school event
Copy a story without a reader
questions.explanation: A notice communicates practical information for a specific audience.

questions.question: Which feature is essential in a formal letter?
questions.explanation: Formal letters conventionally use suitable greetings and closings.

questions.question: Which activity is part of drafting in the writing process?
options: Turn an outline into an initial version of the text
Check only final punctuation after publication
questions.explanation: Drafting develops planned ideas into an initial written text.

questions.question: Which activity is proofreading?
options: Check the final draft for spelling, punctuation and typographical errors
Choose a topic for an essay
questions.explanation: Proofreading focuses on surface-level errors in a near-final text.

questions.question: Which is the main purpose of revising a composition?
options: Change every noun to a pronoun
questions.explanation: Revision addresses content and structure to improve the text.

questions.question: Which approach makes feedback more useful to a learner?
options: Identify a specific strength and give a clear next step
Compare the learner mockingly with peers
Give comments unrelated to the objective
questions.explanation: Specific, constructive feedback tells learners what is working and what to improve.

questions.question: Which assessment is conducted during instruction to guide next steps?
questions.explanation: Formative assessment gathers evidence during learning to inform teaching and feedback.

questions.question: Which assessment is mainly used to summarize achievement at the end of a unit?
questions.explanation: Summative assessment evaluates achievement at the end of a period or unit.
